signature.name: Dealey Plaza
signature.detail: The site of the 1963 assassination of President Kennedy and the most visited historic spot in Dallas. Come early in the morning to walk the plaza and the grassy knoll before crowds arrive; it is free and open to the public.

signature.name: Sixth Floor Museum
signature.detail: Housed in the former Texas School Book Depository, this museum tells the story of the Kennedy assassination with artifacts and the sniper's window view. Book timed tickets online in advance, as entry slots sell out on weekends.

signature.name: Reunion Tower
signature.detail: Dallas's most recognizable skyline landmark, with an observation deck offering sweeping views over the city. Go near sunset for the best light and check the weather before buying tickets, since views depend on clear skies.

signature.name: The Dallas Museum of Art
signature.detail: A major art museum in the Arts District with a wide collection spanning centuries and cultures. General admission is free, making it an easy must-see; check opening days before you go.

signature.name: The Dallas Arboretum and Botanical Garden
signature.detail: Lovely lakeside gardens known for seasonal flower displays. Visit in spring or fall for peak blooms and allow a couple of hours to walk the grounds.

transport: DART light rail $2.50 a ride; rideshares moderate
